component.name: foSSH Console
component.summary: Run website analytics that cannot identify your visitors

description.p: foSSH Console administers a foSSH install: self-hosted website analytics that records what pages were visited without recording who visited them. Your data stays on your own server, and there is no company in the middle — including this project's author.
Most analytics ask you to trade your visitors' privacy for your dashboard. foSSH does not make that trade, and it is not a setting you have to find:

ul.li: No cross-site identity, no cookies, and no device fingerprinting.
No raw IP addresses or user-agent strings kept at rest — ever, not even briefly.
Reported groups are k-anonymised before any part of the program can read them, so a breakdown cannot single out one person.
The component that receives events cannot make an outbound network connection at all. That is enforced by how the software is built, not by a checkbox.

description.p: From this window you can see what each of your sites recorded today, run real queries against the stored aggregates, add external services with an API key, and complete first-run operator setup. It talks to a local helper process over a pipe and never listens on a network socket of its own.
Installing this gives you the administration interface. The analytics server itself is the fossh package, which this depends on.

screenshot.caption: Today's figures and the health of the install at a glance
Queries against the stored aggregates, k-anonymised before they are read
External services you add, with their keys sealed on disk and never shown again
The terms, privacy text and licence, readable inside the application

description.p: The first release of the console, replacing the terminal interface shipped up to 0.1.3. Adds external services authenticated with an API key, and self-healing checks that report problems with the install alongside how to fix each one.
